judgments.reasoning_cat1: The letter concedes the terms "have not always been interpreted and applied consistently" and then defines them as the grandparent "of a Regular Situation Holder or Group I Extra or of his or her spouse at the time the grandparent dies" — step-grandparents, and the temporal qualifier's referent, remain open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a unilateral Times letter furnished under ¶12 (c016) purporting to construe Section 3-P of the surviving 1981-84 booklet (¶14, c018), so its binding force against the Union is itself a whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain non-retroactivity sentence tied to "a death occurring prior to the date hereof"; the only softness is that the letter is undated in the record.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies c031 only, and does not collide with ¶16 (c020) on effectiveness or ¶14 (c018).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The quoted replacement first sentence is garbled and incomplete and the fifth sentence quoted for deletion breaks off mid-clause ("for a later"), so what is actually substituted and what is removed cannot be read from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends Section 13-K.2 of the 1981-84 booklet preserved by ¶14 (c018); deleting the liquidation sentence while leaving accumulation open raises a payout question the rest of the Memorandum does not answer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "certain neutrals", "subject to their availability and willingness to serve" and "effectuate the designation process" identify no one and impose no outcome — an agreement to meet, not to designate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ¶13 (c017) describes this appendix as an executed letter of understanding on "Status Quo" and Merits Arbitrator designations, which this letter does not actually accomplish.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to negotiate "the conditions" triggered by "when the normal daily order reaches 2500 copies" — both the duty and the trigger (normal? whose count? sustained how long?) are indefinite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument defines "normal daily order" or supplies a fallback if negotiations fail; the grievance and arbitration route in ¶3 (c005) is the only backstop.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The assignment obligation is conditioned on "satisfactory arrangements" being "agreed upon" and "in operation" yet also on a thirty-day deadline from a "revised Glen Burnie agreement", and closes with the unquantified "shall not involve The Times in increased costs".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel Edison paragraph (c037) uses the same conditional structure, and the cost proviso echoes c044; the internal condition/deadline tension is within this paragraph rather than against another provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A duty only "to negotiate" that arises after grievances are "resolved satisfactorily" and the plant "is running", with the same open-ended "does not involve The Times in increased costs" proviso.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with c036 on Lancaster magazine transport and with ¶3 (c005) on Edison work assignments, but the two can be read as sequential rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Change '6-1/2%' to '7.678%' to reflect the present welfare contribution percentage" states both a fixed figure and a purpose of reflecting a 'present' rate, inviting argument whether the rate is frozen at 7.678% or floats with the Fund's requirements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with ¶2(a) (c002) ("pension and welfare contributions shall be made on this amount"), the $3.67 deduction in c039 and the Earnings Bonus carve-out in c055 — together these define the contribution base and are the obvious flashpoint in a welfare-fund contribution dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The inserted language is not closed by a quotation mark and the instruction places it "after the words 'per shift' in the first sentence" of a sentence not reproduced, so the resulting text — and whether the $3.67 is an employee deduction or an employer contribution — cannot be determined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ¶2(a) (c002) describes the same $3.67 as "from wages and after taxes ... contributed to the Welfare Fund" with a five-shift maximum absent here, a mismatch that bears directly on what the Fund is owed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dated table of per-shift casual contributions; the first figure is illegible in the text ('§.00'), which is a transcription rather than drafting problem, and "additional" is not defined against what base.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside c038 and c002 in fixing the Welfare Fund contribution obligation; casuals are not otherwise addressed, so no contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise textual insertion ("in writing, at least sixty (60) days prior thereto") with "[balance as in original]"; the only opacity is that the amended sentence is not reproduced.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The immediately following addition (c042) creates an exception to the very sixty-day notice this clause inserts, so the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "This shall only apply to a New York Times part or section regularly inserted" and "the promptest practicable notice" are both open-textured, and "can demonstrate that it did not have sixty (60) days' notice itself" sets no standard of proof.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies c041's flat sixty-day requirement and disclaims modifying "any other notice requirements pursuant to the Contract", leaving the interaction with the surviving 1981-84 booklet (¶14, c018) to be worked out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "a uniform portion of each employee's wage increase" gives the Union an unbounded unilateral diversion right with no cap, no mechanics and no definition of "vacation pay benefit".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Diverting wage increases affects the pension and welfare contribution base fixed by ¶2(a) (c002) and c038, and c044 caps the resulting cost to The Times — a genuine interlock.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "nominal administrative costs" and "fully cooperate ... in developing any such alternatives" are vague standards with no measurable boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies c043 and echoes the "no increased costs" provisos in c036 and c037, but no contrary provision was found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A balanced committee "to study possible methods" — an agreement to study creates no measurable duty, but there is nothing genuinely ambiguous to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Free-standing; no other provision addresses terminally ill employees or benefits for them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is literally incomplete — "it will guarantee all Saturday night Bulldog [ ] uding routes and relays" — so the object of the guarantee is missing, and "so long as it has a Saturday night Bulldog Edition" makes the whole guarantee defeasible at the employer's election.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It touches the bulldog-route returns exception in Appendix B (c028) and the layoff protections in ¶3 (c005), but the defect is chiefly on the face of the text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "notwithstanding any provision to the contrary" overrides unnamed provisions, and the exception for retroactive 1987 wages paid in 1988 is a carve-out whose interaction with the 5.112% rate takes work to follow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against ¶2 (c048), which sets 3.86% for 1988 onward, and against the gross-wages definition in c050, which repeats the same 1988 carve-out — consistent, but only just.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single percentage applied to "gross wages paid the employee by The Times during the applicable year", with "gross wages" defined in ¶4(a); definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits c049, c050 and c052 without friction; the only qualifier is the Union's termination right in c054.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stub-period application of the same 3.86% rate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its payment timing is addressed both by c052 (60 days) and c053 (30 days after March 30, 1993), a mismatch that belongs to those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Gross wages" is anchored to a W-2 box, which is objective, but the exclusions (the Bonus itself, and 1987 retroactive wages paid in 1988) plus a separate-W-2 instruction make the base a natural battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ¶4(b) (c051) immediately adds items that are not on the W-2, so the W-2 anchor is not exhaustive, and ¶8 (c055) treats Bonus payments as outside the fund-contribution base.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "to the extent that such State disability and workers' compensation benefits do not appear on the employee's W-2" is a workable rule, though "those shifts for which an employee receives benefits under The Times Disability Plan" ties two different benefit sources together.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly departs from the W-2 definition in c050, which the drafters signposted with "However", so the two are reconcilable but must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat sixty-day payment deadline keyed to "the applicable bonus period"; nothing ambiguous in isolation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: ¶6 (c053) requires the January 1–March 30, 1993 Bonus to be paid within thirty days after March 30, 1993, and ¶7 (c054) uses sixty days from termination — a direct timing inconsistency with this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It gives the Union an option to add $25.93 to scales "or allocated in the manner set forth in Paragraph 7", but Paragraph 7 is a termination right rather than an allocation mechanism, and "continuation or other disposition" is left undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its thirty-day deadline for the final stub-period Bonus contradicts the sixty-day rule in ¶5 (c052), and its automatic $25.93 conversion overlaps with the Union's independent right in ¶7 (c054).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The tail — "or to any fringe benefit provided under the contract or negotiated by any other union and the Times in connection with the current extension negotiations or at any time through March 30, 1993" — is syntactically tangled, so what the $25.93 may be applied to, and when, is genuinely unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs alongside ¶6 (c053), which also disposes of the $25.93 at the Union's option, and its cross-reference is what ¶6 calls "the manner set forth in Paragraph 7"; the two mechanisms are not cleanly separated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any benefit ... which is calculated on or determined by the employee's wage rate" with an illustrative but non-limiting list, plus "applied so as to eliminate any duplication", sets a broad rule and then a general-versus-specific carve-out for the Welfare and Pension Funds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That final sentence disclaims Welfare and Pension Fund contributions on Bonus payments and on the notional $25.93, which pulls directly against ¶2(a) (c002) ("Pension and welfare contributions shall be made on this amount") and the 7.678%-of-wages formula in c038 — the central contribution-base conflict in this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The number in the first sentence of Paragraph 3 is now eighty-eight (88)" identifies neither what the number counts nor the text it replaces, so the provision is unreadable without an external document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It revises a Memorandum of Understanding at pp. 103-5 of the 1981-84 booklet as changed by a 1984 agreement, both preserved by ¶14 (c018) but not reproduced, so its fit cannot be verified from within.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deleting "the sentence providing for certain floormen being available for driving assignments" identifies the target only by description, so which sentence goes is itself a question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The floor and chauffeur staffing created in Appendix A (c021-c022) and the foreman provision (c014) are affected by removing driving flexibility, though no direct contradiction is stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An internal memorandum describing "present practice" whose text is partly scrambled (one of the three locations is broken across lines) and whose closing sentence — new machines "incorporated into one of the three locations" — states a practice of expansion, not a fixed obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the content given to "present practices" by the Honor Boxes/Vending Machines side letter (c029) via the covering letter, so a descriptive memo is doing operative work; it also bears on the West Side Direct reorganisation right in c026.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Putting "abolition" in quotation marks and preserving "any other agreement contained therein or otherwise regarding those routes other than that portion providing for attrition" makes the residue of the 1983 memorandum genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the flat statement in Appendix B (c026) that the 1983 West Side Direct memorandum "shall be abolished", and ¶14 (c018) would give the Memorandum priority over this later confirming letter — a real reconciliation problem.
